elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"

elements.element: Vendor assigns rights in deliverables to Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation"
"Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3"; Vendor Technology = "Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates..."

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence language in the rendered clause; only the non-operative comment asserts "13.2 gives us the embedded-IP licence", which is not supplied for review

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: Rendered clause is silent on Customer Data; only the definition notes "Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data"
"Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable" with full assignment of "all right, title, and interest"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: Clause vests ownership of Deliverables in Customer; no operative statement of Vendor ownership of generic tools/know-how (only the Deliverable definition's exclusion)

elements.element: Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables
elements.evidence: The prior licence sentence was deleted and no replacement licence grant appears: "Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3."

offending_extra_words: Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3.
reasons: Ownership and assignment legs of the preferred position are cleanly achieved: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable" plus "Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns... all right, title, and interest".

The preferred level is incomplete on the record: the embedded Vendor IP licence (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free) and Customer's retention of all rights in Customer Data appear nowhere in the operative text; the margin comment's reference to 13.2 is non-operative and unverifiable.

Fallback is not satisfied either — no Vendor ownership of generic tools/know-how and, critically, the deleted licence sentence leaves Customer with no use/modify/sublicense grant if ownership language were ever narrowed.

Minimality fails: the deterministic gate records a 0.736 changed-character ratio against the 0.600 limit, and the added sentence "Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3" duplicates protection already given to Vendor by 14.3 — an operator flip ("Customer" for "Vendor") plus a short assignment insertion would suffice.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, contradiction, or dangling mechanic; the revoked, term-limited licence it replaces was adverse to us and its removal creates no gap given outright ownership.
